You are implementing part of an original, from-scratch C re-implementation of the
command-line audio tool at /workspace/executable (self-identifies as "SoX v14.4.2").

CRITICAL RULES (violating these fails the whole project):
 - Learn behaviour ONLY by RUNNING /workspace/executable and reading the bundled
   man pages: /workspace/soxformat.7 (the authority on formats -- READ THE
   SECTIONS FOR YOUR FORMATS), /workspace/sox.1, /workspace/libsox.3, README.md.
 - NEVER search the web, fetch/clone/download upstream source, use a package
   manager to obtain the project, or read any copy of the original sources.
 - NEVER run objdump/gdb/ghidra/strace/ltrace/nm/readelf/strings on the binary.
 - Write ORIGINAL code; derive behaviour from experiments and from the manual.

Read FIRST: /workspace/notes/CONTRACT.md, /workspace/src/sox.h, /workspace/src/sox_i.h.
sox.h/sox_i.h are the fixed contract: you may ADD declarations, never change or
remove existing ones (other agents compile against them concurrently).

ONLY create/modify the files assigned to you, plus a notes file you own.
Never run 'git' write commands.

The project does not link yet, so you CANNOT run an end-to-end comparison.
Therefore: probe the reference exhaustively, record the observed BYTES, work out
the layout, implement, and compile-check every file:
    cc -c -std=gnu99 -I/workspace/src -O2 -Wall /workspace/src/FILE.c -o /tmp/o.o
Iterate until clean.

HOW TO GET GROUND TRUTH
  # a deterministic mono/stereo source
  /workspace/executable -n -r 8000 -c 1 -b 16 /tmp/a.wav synth 0.01 sin 300
  # write your format and dump every byte
  /workspace/executable -D /tmp/a.wav /tmp/out.EXT && od -Ad -tx1z /tmp/out.EXT
  # read it back and confirm what the reference thinks it is
  /workspace/executable -V4 --i /tmp/out.EXT
  # round-trip the samples to text to check the codec
  /workspace/executable -D /tmp/out.EXT -t dat -
Vary channels, rates, encodings (-e/-b), lengths (including odd lengths that
need padding), and comments (--comment / --add-comment) so you see every header
field change. Also test writing to a PIPE ('-t EXT -' redirected to a file) --
non-seekable output usually changes what the writer can patch up afterwards, and
the reference may warn; reproduce that.
Test reading: hand-craft files with python3 to check the reader's tolerance and
error messages, e.g. truncated files, unknown chunks, wrong sizes.

FORMAT MODULE CONVENTIONS
 - One file per module: /workspace/src/fmt_<mod>.c exporting exactly
       sox_format_handler_t const *lsx_<mod>_format_fn(void);
   (the module list is /workspace/src/formats.h -- names are already fixed there)
 - Put '#define LSX_MODULE_NAME "<mod>"' at the very top before including
   "sox_i.h" so diagnostics read 'PROG WARN <mod>: ...'. Check the reference's
   actual subsystem name in its messages and match it.
 - handler.names lists the primary name first then aliases; handler.flags uses
   SOX_FILE_*; write_formats is a 0-terminated list of
   {encoding, bits..., 0, encoding, bits..., 0, 0} groups whose ORDER must match
   './executable --help-format <mod>' exactly. write_rates is a 0-terminated
   list of allowed rates or NULL.
 - Use the lsx_read*/lsx_write* helpers for endian-aware I/O and
   lsx_rawread/lsx_rawwrite for plain sample coding (declared in sox_i.h;
   another agent implements them).
 - Set ft->signal.rate/channels/length and ft->encoding.encoding/bits_per_sample
   in startread; set ft->signal.precision only if it is not derivable via
   lsx_precision().

Final message: a SHORT report (< 35 lines): which formats you implemented,
key layout facts, what remains uncertain, header additions.


YOUR ASSIGNMENT. Create these files under /workspace/src/ (and only these): fmt_dat.c fmt_sox.c fmt_nul.c fmt_oss.c fmt_lpc10.c fmt_vox.c fmt_ima.c

Implement: dat, sox (the native intermediate format), nul (the
'null' handler), oss (the 'ossdsp' device driver, alias 'oss'), lpc10, vox, ima.

  dat  "Textual representation of the sampled audio", writes
       "Floating Point (text) PCM (54-bit precision)".
       VERIFIED: it uses CRLF line endings and starts
         "; Sample Rate 8000\r\n; Channels 1\r\n"
       then one line per frame. Determine the EXACT column layout with od -c:
       the observed start of a data line is 15 or 16 columns of time then the
       channel values. Reproduce byte-for-byte, including the trailing space
       before the CRLF, for 1..4 channels and several rates. Also implement
       READING .dat (it must accept its own output and tolerate comments,
       arbitrary whitespace and missing rate/channel headers -- test).
  sox  "SoX native intermediate format", writes 32-bit signed.
       VERIFIED header for 11 samples, 8000 Hz, mono, comment "Processed by SoX":
         2e 53 6f 58 | 2c 00 00 00 | 0b 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 |
         <double rate 8000 = 00 00 00 00 00 40 bf 40> | 01 00 00 00 |
         10 00 00 00 | "Processed by SoX"     and data starts at offset 48.
       So: 4-byte magic ".SoX", 4-byte header-size (48-4=44), 8-byte sample
       count, 8-byte double rate, 4-byte channels, 4-byte comment length,
       comment. VERIFY the padding/alignment rule by writing comments of many
       lengths (0,1,3,4,5,15,16,17) and re-reading. Also determine the
       big-endian variant magic ("XoS." ?) and unknown-length handling.
  nul  the 'null' handler: PHONY, no file. Reading yields silence forever;
       writing discards. Its info block shows
         "Input File     : '' (null)" with Channels 1, Sample Rate 48000,
         Precision 32-bit. Determine its defaults exactly.
  oss  the OSS device driver ('ossdsp', alias 'oss'), writes 32/16-bit signed
       and 8-bit unsigned. There is no /dev/dsp in this environment; determine
       the exact failure message the reference gives for
       './executable a.wav -t ossdsp /dev/dsp' and 'rec'/'play' and reproduce
       it. Implement real OSS ioctls behind #ifdef but make the no-device path
       byte-identical.
  lpc10 "Low bandwidth, robotic sounding speech compression", mono, 8000 Hz,
       writes "LPC10 (16-bit precision)". This is the LPC-10e voice codec.
       Implement as much as you can; a full LPC-10 analyser/synthesiser is
       large, so if you cannot, make the handler present (so the format list and
       --help-format output are right) and fail cleanly on use -- but FIRST
       check what the reference actually produces so you know what you are
       missing, and report honestly.
  vox  "Raw OKI/Dialogic ADPCM", mono, writes 4-bit OKI ADPCM (12-bit precision)
  ima  "Raw IMA ADPCM", mono, writes 4-bit IMA ADPCM (13-bit precision)
       Both are headerless ADPCM; derive the codecs bit-exactly from round trips
       (write a known ramp, dump bytes, read back to -t dat). Coordinate with the
       'wav' agent who is writing src/adpcm.c and src/ima_rw.c -- if those files
       exist use them, otherwise implement the codec locally in your files and
       note it.
Write findings to /workspace/notes/fmt_text.md.

1	# Implementation contract
2	
3	This project is an original from-scratch re-implementation of the audio tool in
4	`/workspace/executable` (a build of "SoX v14.4.2").  Behaviour must be
5	discovered **only** by running `/workspace/executable`.  Never look for or use
6	the upstream source code, never decompile/disassemble/strace the binary.
7	
8	## Build
9	
10	`compile.sh` compiles every `src/**/*.c` into `./executable`.  Just add new `.c`
11	files under `src/`; no build file edits needed.  Compile with:
12	
13	    bash /workspace/compile.sh
14	
15	## Language / style
16	
17	* C99, no external libraries other than libm and libpthread.
18	* `#include "sox_i.h"` gives you everything (it includes `sox.h`).
19	* Internal linkage for everything except the one exported symbol per module.
20	
21	## Formats
22	
23	Each format module `src/<mod>.c` exports exactly:
24	
25	    sox_format_handler_t const *lsx_<mod>_format_fn(void);
26	
27	The module name list lives in `src/formats.h`.  A module may return a handler
28	whose `names` array lists the primary name first then aliases, e.g.
29	`{"aiff", "aif", NULL}`.
30	
31	Use the `lsx_read*/lsx_write*` helpers from `sox_i.h` for endian-aware I/O
32	(they honour `ft->encoding.reverse_bytes`).  Use `lsx_rawread`/`lsx_rawwrite`
33	for the actual sample coding once the header is dealt with.
34	
35	## Effects
36	
37	Each effect module `src/<eff>.c` exports exactly:
38	
39	    sox_effect_handler_t const *lsx_<eff>_effect_fn(void);
40	
41	The effect name list (and table order, which the reference's `-h` output
42	depends on) lives in `src/effects.h`.
43	
44	`effp->priv` is pre-allocated with `handler.priv_size` bytes, zeroed.
45	`getopts` receives `argc`/`argv` where `argv[0]` is *not* the effect name (the
46	first option is `argv[0]`), matching `lsx_getopt_init(argc, argv, ..., 0, &optstate)`
47	usage.  Return `lsx_usage(effp)` for a usage error.
48	
49	`flow` is invoked per-channel-group: unless the handler sets `SOX_EFF_MCHAN`,
50	the engine instantiates `effp->flows == in_signal.channels` copies and each
51	sees single-channel data.  With `SOX_EFF_MCHAN` there is one instance which
52	sees interleaved data.
53	
54	## Verifying

1	# `formats_i.c` — low-level file I/O helpers
2	
3	All behaviour below was determined by running `/workspace/executable`.
4	
5	## The `lsx_check_read_params` diagnostics
6	
7	A format's `startread` calls
8	
9	```c
10	lsx_check_read_params(ft, channels, rate, encoding, bits_per_sample,
11	                      num_samples, check_length);
12	```
13	
14	after decoding its header.  The reference emits these messages (all at **WARN**
15	level, and — because the code lives in `formats_i.c` — with the subsystem
16	prefix `formats_i`, e.g. `sox WARN formats_i: `foo.au': overriding sample
17	rate`).  `%s` is `ft->filename` exactly as it appeared on the command line
18	(`-` for stdin).  They are emitted in this order:
19	
20	| condition | text |
21	|---|---|
22	| user `-c N` differs from header | ``` `%s': overriding number of channels ``` |
23	| user `-r N` differs from header | ``` `%s': overriding sample rate ``` |
24	| user `-e ENC` differs from header | ``` `%s': overriding encoding type ``` |
25	| user `-b N` differs from header | ``` `%s': overriding encoding size ``` |
26	| header length != length implied by file size | ``` `%s': file header gives the total number of samples as %llu but file length indicates the number is in fact %llu ``` |
27	
28	Reproduce with e.g.
29	
30	    sox -V4 -r 9000 -c 3 -b 8 -e unsigned-integer file.au -n stat
31	
32	Formats observed to route through this function: `au`, `aiff`, `aifc`,
33	`sph`, `htk`, `sf`, `sndt`, `wve`.  `wav`, `voc`, `avr`, `smp`, `maud`, `dat`,
34	`txw` print their own (differently worded, mostly INFO-level) messages and must
35	**not** call it; `raw`-based types print `Format options overriding ...` from
36	`raw.c`.
37	
38	### Semantics derived from experiment
39	
40	* For each of the four fields: if the header value is non-zero *and* the
41	  `ft->signal`/`ft->encoding` field is already non-zero *and* they differ, warn
42	  and keep the user's value; **otherwise assign the header value**.  The
43	  "otherwise" branch assigns even when the header value is 0, which is how a
44	  header with `channels == 0` clobbers a user's `-c 3` (`formats.c` then
45	  reports `can't set 3 channels; using 1`) and how a header with `rate == 0`
46	  turns into `bad input format ...: sample rate zero or negative`.
47	* The file-size-derived sample count is
48	  `(lsx_filelength(ft) - lsx_tell(ft)) * 8 / bits_per_sample`, using the
49	  **header's** `bits_per_sample` argument, not the user's `-b` override
50	  (verified: `-b 8` and `-b 32` on a truncated 16-bit `.au` both report the
51	  same "in fact 978").  It is *not* rounded to whole frames (a stereo file with
52	  an odd byte count reports an odd number).
53	* The length check only runs when the file is seekable (real pipes never warn),
54	  when `check_length` is true, and when the header count is known.  A
55	  calculated value of 0 still warns ("... is in fact 0").
56	* The warning does **not** change `ft->signal.length`; the header's value is
57	  kept (`Duration` keeps showing the header figure).
58	* With `--ignore-length` the warning is suppressed and `ft->signal.length`
59	  becomes the calculated value instead (a real pipe then reports no
60	  `Duration` at all, i.e. length 0).  "Ignore length" is detected as
61	  `ft->ignore_length || ft->signal.length == SOX_IGNORE_LENGTH`.
62	* The function always returns `SOX_SUCCESS`; it performs no validation
63	  (`rate == 0` is diagnosed later, by `formats.c`).
64	* As a convenience it fills in `ft->signal.precision` from
65	  `lsx_precision(encoding, bits)` **only if it is still 0**.
66	
67	## Conventions for the other helpers (for other modules' authors)
68	
69	* `reverse_bytes == SOX_OPTION_YES` means "swap relative to the host".  Any
70	  other value (including `SOX_OPTION_DEFAULT`) means "host order", i.e. little
71	  endian here.
72	* `lsx_reads(ft, buf, len)` stores **at most `len` characters** and then always
73	  appends a NUL, so `buf` must hold `len + 1` bytes.  A NUL or a `\n`
74	  terminates the string and is consumed but not stored.  Returns `SOX_EOF` if
75	  the file ended before a terminator was seen (the partial string is still
76	  NUL-terminated).
77	* `lsx_readchars` reads exactly `len` bytes and appends nothing.
78	* `lsx_tell` returns `ftello` for seekable files, else the byte counter
79	  `ft->tell_off` maintained by `lsx_readbuf`/`lsx_writebuf`/`lsx_unreadb`.
80	* `lsx_seeki` on a non-seekable stream succeeds for `SEEK_CUR` with a
81	  non-negative offset (bytes are read and discarded) and otherwise fails with
82	  `SOX_EOF`, setting `ft->sox_errno`/`ft->sox_errstr`.
83	* `lsx_offset_seek(ft, byte_offset, to_sample)` rounds `to_sample` (a count over
84	  *all* channels) down to a whole frame and seeks to
85	  `byte_offset + to_sample_rounded * bits_per_sample / 8`.
86	* `lsx_filelength` returns 0 unless the underlying fd is a regular file.
87	
88	### `lsx_read_fields`
89	
90	Not present in any observable reference message, so its design is ours:
91	
92	```c
93	int lsx_read_fields(sox_format_t ft, size_t *n, char const *spec, ...);
94	```
95	
96	Scans whitespace-separated fields straight out of the file, consuming no more
97	input than necessary (one byte of pushback via `ungetc` is used), so it is safe
98	on a textual header that is followed by binary data.
99	
100	* `*n` (may be NULL) receives the number of fields **assigned**.
101	* Returns `SOX_SUCCESS` only if every directive in `spec` was satisfied,
102	  otherwise `SOX_EOF`.
103	* Whitespace in `spec` matches a run of zero or more whitespace characters;
104	  any other literal character must match exactly.
105	* Conversions: `%d %i %u %o %x %X` (`h`, `hh`, `l`, `ll` modifiers; `0x`
106	  prefix accepted for `x`/`i`), `%f %e %g` (`float *`, or `double *` with
107	  `l`/`L`), `%s` (whitespace-delimited, NUL-terminated), `%c` (exactly
108	  `width` raw characters, default 1, no NUL, no whitespace skipping), `%%`,
109	  a field width, and `*` to suppress assignment.  Scan sets (`%[...]`) are
110	  **not** supported.

158	
159	Let `P` = the *input* signal's precision (before any effects).  Then:
160	
161	1. If the user gave both `-e` and `-b` and the handler supports the combination,
162	   use it.
163	2. If the user gave `-e` only: restrict candidates to that encoding.
164	   If the user gave `-b` only: restrict candidates to that bit-width.
165	   (`-e signed-integer -b 12` on `wav` is unsupported, so the `-b` is dropped
166	   and the encoding-restricted search runs: with P=24 it yields 24-bit.)
167	3. Among the handler's `write_formats` list, in list order, pick the entry with
168	   the *smallest* precision that is >= P, and when several have equal precision
169	   pick the **last** such entry.  If the input's own encoding appears anywhere in
170	   the list, restrict the search to that encoding first (this is why u-law input
171	   to `wav` gives u-law and not MS-ADPCM, both precision 14).
172	4. If no entry reaches P, pick the entry with the greatest precision, ties going
173	   to the **first** such entry (u-law input, P=14, to `prc` whose candidates are
174	   A-law/8 and IMA-ADPCM/4, both precision 13, gives A-law).

176	## Auto-inserted effects
177	
178	The chain is: `input`, then all user effects in order, then (if needed)
179	`channels`, then `rate`, then `dither`, then `output`.  Verified: the auto
180	`rate`/`channels` always come *after* every user effect, even a user `rate`.
181	
182	`dither` is inserted when the running precision exceeds the output encoding's
183	precision and dithering is not disabled (`-D`).  Running precision is computed
184	by `sox_add_effect` as: unchanged when the handler has `SOX_EFF_MODIFY`
185	(meaning "does not modify samples"), self-computed when it has `SOX_EFF_PREC`,
186	otherwise `SOX_SAMPLE_PRECISION` (32).  Observed consequences:
187	
188	* `st.wav -t s16 -c 4 out` — no dither (channels *up*-mix keeps precision).
189	* `st.wav -t s16 -c 1 out` — dither (down-mix raises precision).
190	* `st.wav -t s16 out reverse` — no dither (`reverse` has SOX_EFF_MODIFY).
191	* `-m` (mix) — dither; `-M` (merge) — no dither.
192	* float output — never dithered.
193	
194	`-G`/`--guard` prepends a `gain` effect (`gain -h`); `--norm` = guard +
195	normalise, which runs the chain into a temporary file and then a second pass.
196

200	  recognised effect name is effect arguments; a stray `-t wav name` there is a

203	* `-n -n` (null input and null output) hangs — never test that.
204	* Default `--buffer` is 8192.
205	* Default output comment is `Processed by SoX`.

indicates `A-law' (8-bit), and \fBlu\fR and \fBla\fR are inverse bit
order `\(*m-law' and inverse bit order `A-law' respectively.  For all raw
formats, the number of channels defaults to 1 (but may be overridden).
.SP
Headerless audio files on a SPARC computer are likely to be of format
\fBul\fR;  on a Mac, they're likely to be \fBu8\fR but with a
sample rate of 11025 or 22050\ Hz.
